transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Lopez (Redwood SE), Sanjay Rao (Verdant VP Procurement), Lena Ortiz (Verdant Legal), Markus Chen (Verdant Platform)

Auto-summary: Quick legal+procurement alignment focused on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets and pricing committee timing. Agreed next steps for redlines, security docs, and pilot preflight.

00:00 Ethan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, um, objective is to align on contract redlines and get the pilot gating nailed so your pricing committee has what they need.
00:18 Sanjay Rao: Great thanks Ethan, we have Lena and Markus here, Lena is our legal lead, Markus will handle technical preflight — we want to know if Redwood can hit our 99th percentile latency at 300ms for conversational flows and how pricing will look at our expected throughput.
00:34 Maya Lopez: Quick clarifying note — when you say 300ms 99th, is that token gen or end-to-end including network? because that changes the routing and the Dedicated sizing.
00:48 Markus Chen: Sorry, yeah end-to-end, user-facing; we also have a requirement that keys live in our KMS and SSO must be SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning.
01:05 Lena Ortiz: From legal, our main asks are DPA data residency clauses and a limited liability cap for PII incidents. We can be flexible, but want the DPA to reference SOC2 and specify retention windows.
01:22 Ethan Park: Understood. We'll share the annotated MSA and DPA redline after the call. To set expectations, Redwood offers hosted and dedicated tiers; data residency and KMS-integration are common — dedicated with customer-managed KMS is feasible in Private deployments, and for hosted we have KMS key-wrapping options.
01:45 Sanjay Rao: Okay, so team — in terms of procurement, we need the final redline before our pricing committee on Friday, tentatively 2025-05-23. We need cost estimates for both hosted and dedicated paths.
01:58 Ethan Park: We'll provide both line-item cost models. Maya, can you remind them about batching/caching and how that impacts token cost?
02:09 Maya Lopez: Yep — there's two levers: batching and KV cache prefixing. For chat-type workloads we can shave unit cost by 15-30% depending on cache hit rate. Note: batch windows can add 10-40ms latency; we tune per-route. Also, quantization profiles can reduce GPU footprint but can affect some quality metrics — we'll surface recommended profile per workload.
02:38 Markus Chen: That-- that tradeoff is fine as long as 99th stays near our target. Any fallback if dedicated capacity spikes?
02:47 Ethan Park: Yes, smart routing can failover to a compatible variant — for example a slightly higher-latency but lower-cost fallback. We'll document SLOs for primary and fallback tiers.
02:58 Lena Ortiz: On the DPA, do you have precedent language for subprocessor lists and audit rights? We need to know if Redwood will permit onsite audits or an SOC2 + bridge letter.
03:13 Ethan Park: SOC2 plus a bridge letter is typical; onsite audits are rare and usually handled through certs. We'll attach our SOC2 report and a vendor compliance pack.
03:25 Sanjay Rao: Pricing committee wants to understand penalty language tied to SLAs, e.g., credits if 99th exceeds threshold for multiple days.
03:36 Maya Lopez: We can propose a credit model — typically volume-based credits rather than monetary fines, but we can do an SLA credit schedule in the MSA. I'll draft a sample.
03:48 Lena Ortiz: We also need clarity on egress fees and data export pathways — do you support VPC peering and private egress?
03:56 Ethan Park: Yes, VPC peering and private link options exist for Private deployments; egress fees depend on region and egress volume. We'll give typical egress scenarios in the cost model.
04:10 Markus Chen: Technical thing — for pilot, we'd like a small POC that runs 10k qps over two weeks, but that's probably too big? that was a slip — 10k requests per day, sorry.
04:22 Maya Lopez: 10k/day is fine for a pilot. We'll recommend a pilot window and a smoke benchmark. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; if you require HSM-backend we need to align on the key wrapping flow.
04:40 Lena Ortiz: Also: retention windows — our policy is 30 days of raw logs then purge unless explicitly retained. Can that be accommodated?
04:49 Ethan Park: Yes, retention is configurable for Private deployments; hosted has standard retention with options for extended retention as an add-on. We'll call that out in the DPA.
04:58 Sanjay Rao: Quick question — do you support contractual data residency per-region? For EU data we need it to stay in eu-west-1.
05:08 Ethan Park: Yes, region pinning is supported on Dedicated/Private; hosted API can be region-targeted but with less strict guarantees unless you pick Dedicated.
05:18 Lena Ortiz: On indemnity and caps: are you open to a mutual cap or a carve-out for gross negligence?
05:26 Ethan Park: Standard approach is mutual liability cap tied to fees over 12 months with carve-outs for willful misconduct. We'll propose language.
05:36 Sanjay Rao: Great. For the pricing committee, can you produce a two-path cost sheet: minimum committed Dedicated cost + hosted overage model?
05:45 Ethan Park: Yes. We'll also include an example cost delta assuming 25% KV cache hit rate and 50% batching gain.
05:55 Markus Chen: Actionable ask — before we lock pricing we need a simple benchmark run: 1) 99th latency test, 2) throughput profile, 3) KMS integration smoke. Can Redwood run that against our test VPC?
06:10 Maya Lopez: Yes — subject to onboarding, we can run a constrained benchmark against a private preview. We'll need network ACLs and an engineer contact; Markus is that you?
06:18 Markus Chen: Yep I'll own that. I'll send IP allowlist and a service account.
06:23 Ethan Park: Cool. So to recap next steps: Ethan sends MSA/DPA redline & SOC2 pack by Tue 5/20; Maya uploads pilot runbook and integration notes by 5/23; Verdant confirms pricing committee date by 5/22; Markus provides network details to kick off pilot preflight.
06:44 Lena Ortiz: One last thing — can you include a short section in the DPA about PCI/PHI handling even if not in scope? helps our internal reviewers.
06:53 Ethan Park: We'll include a scoped note for PHI/PCI handling and where we'd recommend using Private deployment + HSM.
07:02 Sanjay Rao: Thanks all, we'll await the redline. If we get the doc by Tue our pricing folks can run the Friday committee. Good run, thanks.
07:12 Ethan Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kick-off once the PRD is shared.
07:20 (call ends)

Notes/attachments mentioned: https://redwood.example.com/security/dpa (security pack), link to pricing spreadsheet (shared in chat), pilot runbook (to be uploaded to shared drive).

Transcript notes: occasional word swaps (e.g., K V cash for KV cache), speaker attribution is rough in a few places, timestamps approximate.
